extractor_claim: Each PC AYA member starts with a little-endian four-byte compressed-length prefix.
comparison: The complete 1,361-file measurement and fail-closed observer confirm this framing.

extractor_claim: Members repeat to physical EOF and their inflated bytes concatenate in member order.
comparison: Current tooling makes EOF termination and ordered concatenation explicit and validates each zlib member.

extractor_claim: The comment claims BEA itself could handle only 1 MiB of uncompressed data at a time.
comparison: There are 364 full 1 MiB members, supporting a writer policy, but no cited runtime/source evidence proves an engine limit.
priority_follow_up: P3: recover writer or loader evidence before assigning causality.

extractor_claim: The extractor allocates exactly 1 MiB for each inflated member.
comparison: The current observer uses aggregate and per-member bounds, streams every member, and is not constrained to a 1 MiB result buffer.

extractor_claim: The extractor caps the concatenated result implicitly at a fixed 4 MiB array.
comparison: Current tools bound output at 128 MiB and append dynamically; 4 MiB is an extractor implementation limit, not a format limit.

extractor_claim: The C++/CLI zlib bridge copies compressed input and output through two fixed 1 MiB native buffers.
comparison: Current Python/.NET readers avoid this bridge; the source also leaks both allocations and does not reject compressed input over 1 MiB.

extractor_claim: AYA members use zlib's standard wrapped uncompress operation.
comparison: Corpus decoding and the pristine executable's imported uncompress thunk corroborate RFC-1950-wrapped zlib.

extractor_claim: Malformed prefixes stop the loop, but several framing failures can still return partial output because only zlib errors set error nonzero.
comparison: The current observer has closed terminal rejection categories for truncation, overrun, zero length, incomplete streams, trailing bytes, and limits.

extractor_claim: The extractor is explicitly PC-only; Xbox/PS2 are unsupported, and Steam equivalence was only assumed.
comparison: Current tooling measures PC and Xbox as distinct envelopes and packaging surfaces; the extractor's target claim is a tool boundary, not cross-platform format evidence.

extractor_claim: The build is net6.0-windows WinForms and x86 because the native mixed-mode projects did not work in Any CPU/x64.
comparison: The retained harness remains x86 solely to load the mixed-mode extractor assemblies; this says nothing about AYA data width.

extractor_claim: The importer starts at stream offset 8, skips four more bytes, and does not validate the CMSH root tag or declared root length.
comparison: Current parsers require CMSH and an exact 372-byte root payload before reading fields.

extractor_claim: Texture count is u32 little-endian at stream offset 0x0C (CMSH payload +0x04).
comparison: All current parser owners read the same offset and corpus-bound the count.

extractor_claim: The 28 bytes after texture count are skipped without names.
comparison: Current round-trip tooling preserves all 60 otherwise-unread root bytes and records that shipped values are nonzero, rather than calling them pointers/reserved.
priority_follow_up: P4: field naming remains a retail-consumer question, not an extractor defect.

extractor_claim: Mesh name is a fixed 300-byte NUL-trimmed UTF-8 field at stream offset 0x2C.
comparison: Current parsers use the same fixed field with stricter identity/path validation.

extractor_claim: Part count is u32 little-endian at stream offset 0x164 (CMSH payload +0x15C).
comparison: Current parsers validate the same offset and require one MESP per declared part.

extractor_claim: Five u32 words after part count are skipped before CMST.
comparison: Current tooling carries the full root payload byte-exactly instead of assuming skipped words are pointers.
priority_follow_up: P4: retain as opaque until exact consumers are joined.

extractor_claim: Every nested record is treated as a four-byte tag plus four-byte little-endian payload length.
comparison: The 367-stream gate validates complete tag framing and lengths.

extractor_claim: ReadTag advances eight bytes but normally ignores declared payload lengths, relying on hard-coded layouts and order.
comparison: Current parsers enforce each known payload length, full record consumption, bounds, and complete accepted orders.

extractor_claim: CMST payload length is numTextures times 36 bytes, then exactly numTextures MSHT records follow.
comparison: All 367 streams obey this framing; current tools retain the 36-byte entries as opaque data.

extractor_claim: Each MSHT contains one TEXB record in that order.
comparison: Current parsers require exact MSHT/TEXB nesting and lengths.

extractor_claim: TEXB begins with 20 bytes described tentatively as used-region/scale metadata.
comparison: Current tools preserve these 20 bytes but deliberately do not interpret them; the extractor's scale/region label is unverified.
priority_follow_up: P3: join a TEXB consumer before naming the 20 bytes.

extractor_claim: TEXB ends in a fixed 128-byte NUL-trimmed texture name.
comparison: Current parsers decode and preserve the same field across the complete stream set.

extractor_claim: Exactly partCount MESP wrappers are consumed, each beginning with CMSP.
comparison: Current parsers require exact MESP cardinality and a 316-byte CMSP child.

extractor_claim: CMSP stores current orientation, base orientation, offset/current position, and base position as 48/48/16/16 bytes in that order.
comparison: Current parsers retain all four blocks and avoid conflating stored-current with runtime-composed transforms.

extractor_claim: Eight bytes after the transforms are called pointers and skipped.
comparison: Current tools carry these words as opaque; pointer semantics are not proved for serialized bytes.
priority_follow_up: P4: keep opaque until loader writes/reads are closed.

extractor_claim: CMSP contains part number, part type, and child count as three u32 values at +0x88.
comparison: Current tools validate identity, type range, child bounds, and cross-check CHLD presence.

extractor_claim: CMSP contains dVert, pVert, triangle, aFrame, vFrame, hFrame, and bone counts at +0xA8.
comparison: Current tools measure frame populations and bind vFrames/hFrames/bones to their records; aFrames remains unnamed.
priority_follow_up: P3: close aFrames at the retail loader before renaming it.

extractor_claim: Six u32 words after the count block and sixteen more u32 words after the 32-byte name are skipped as pointer/unknown data.
comparison: Current round-trip parsing carries all opaque CMSP bytes and measures nonzero contents instead of assigning pointer semantics.
priority_follow_up: P4: field naming only with exact consumers.

extractor_claim: Part name is a fixed 32-byte NUL-trimmed string at CMSP +0xDC.
comparison: Current parser validates termination and UTF-8 over all shipped parts.

extractor_claim: Part records are consumed in a single optional sequence: CHLD, PRNT, NMIC, BBOX, VHFM, HORI, HPOS, HFOV, BONE, BONW, BONS, PBKT, CPOS, CORI, REFR, PMVB.
comparison: Current corpus work enumerates and tests complete observed orders, including variants the extractor's linear optional walk only accepts accidentally.

extractor_claim: CHLD is childCount u32 part indices.
comparison: Current tools bounds-check indices and hierarchy reciprocity/cycles.

extractor_claim: PRNT is one u32 parent part index.
comparison: Current tools validate range and reciprocal CHLD ownership.

extractor_claim: NMIC is one u32 value that the extractor names a next-part-in-chain index.
comparison: Two occurrences in one mesh corroborate only the four-byte, in-range part-index shape; no current consumer evidence proves next-chain behavior.
priority_follow_up: P4: locate the retail NMIC consumer before naming behavior.

extractor_claim: BBOX is an outer BBOX record containing a second BBOX chunk with a 40-byte payload.
comparison: Current parser requires the nested structure and preserves two non-padding words.

extractor_claim: The nested BBOX payload is treated as two vec4-like blocks followed by valid and radius words.
comparison: Current parsing resolves float3 center, carried word, float3 half-extents, carried word, validity, and radius rather than calling both fourth words padding.

extractor_claim: The comment speculates that the repeated BBOX tag is an exporter bug.
comparison: The repeated wrapper is universal measured structure, but no writer evidence proves a bug or accident.
priority_follow_up: P4: do not repeat the bug claim without writer/source evidence.

extractor_claim: VHFM payload length equals numVFrames bytes.
comparison: Current work proves each byte selects an in-range hierarchy pose and measures nontrivial maps.

extractor_claim: HORI payload length equals numHFrames times 48 bytes (three vec4 rows per pose).
comparison: Current parser decodes finite pose rows while retaining the fourth words as authored data.

extractor_claim: HPOS payload length equals numHFrames times 16 bytes.
comparison: Current parser decodes float3 positions and retains the fourth word.

extractor_claim: HFOV payload length equals numHFrames times four bytes.
comparison: Current work measures all 17 camera values and the bounded retail consumer.

extractor_claim: BONE payload length equals numBones u32 words.
comparison: Current work proves each word is an in-range same-mesh part index and measures the seven carriers.

extractor_claim: BONW is skipped as numPVert times four bytes times numBones.
comparison: BONW is absent from the complete measured tag census and current parser rejects it; the formula has no present corpus corroboration.
priority_follow_up: P4: no implementation work until a hash-pinned specimen or writer proves BONW.

extractor_claim: BONS is skipped as numPVert times twelve bytes times numBones.
comparison: BONS is absent from the complete measured tag census and current parser rejects it; the formula has no present corpus corroboration.
priority_follow_up: P4: no implementation work until a hash-pinned specimen or writer proves BONS.

extractor_claim: PBKT is skipped using its own declared chunk length.
comparison: Current parser bounds and byte-round-trips PBKT but explicitly leaves semantics opaque.
priority_follow_up: P2: PB-family schema remains an actual gap; join one instance to its consumer.

extractor_claim: CPOS is skipped using its declared chunk length.
comparison: Current tools identify CPOS as a derived model-space position cache indexed by virtual frame and cross-check it approximately.

extractor_claim: CORI is skipped using its declared chunk length.
comparison: Current tools identify CORI as a derived model-space orientation cache indexed by virtual frame and cross-check it approximately.

extractor_claim: REFR payload is one referenced-part u32 index, normally targeting an earlier part.
comparison: Current tools prove 388 occurrences, require an earlier direct geometry owner, reject chains/ambiguity, and preserve file-versus-expanded views.

extractor_claim: REFR expansion re-reads the target PMVB bytes but applies the referring part's base position/orientation, exemplified by guncrab legs.
comparison: Current tooling resolves repeated geometry with validated graphs and independent transforms without treating the guncrab example as universal semantics.

extractor_claim: A fixed 1,000-entry partVBBookmark array is the extractor's maximum referenceable part table.
comparison: Current bounded parsers use an explicit 256-part profile; neither number is a serialized format maximum.

extractor_claim: After a part, a recognized next-owner marker is rewound by eight bytes for the outer reader; any unrecognized tag is logged unexpected.
comparison: Current parsers enumerate complete measured post-body sibling orders, include CEMT and PMS2/PMSH, and require exact residue accounting instead of a loose marker allowlist.

extractor_claim: CCUS is accepted as a post-part next-owner marker.
comparison: CCUS is absent from the complete measured tag census and every supported post-body sibling order; no hash-pinned specimen currently corroborates it.
priority_follow_up: P4: do not admit CCUS without a hash-pinned specimen or writer/consumer.

extractor_claim: CAMD is accepted as a post-part next-owner marker.
comparison: CAMD occurs 61 times in 61 measured files; current tools accept it only in complete observed orders with BBOX and the measured optional CEMT/PMS2-or-PMSH siblings.

extractor_claim: PMVB begins with a 296-byte CMVB owner; group count is byte +264 and stride/FVF/topology are u32 values at +276/+280/+284.
comparison: Current parser proves the payload length/offsets and measures supported triples rather than merely reading them.

extractor_claim: The extractor calls the CMVB group-count byte numTextures and iterates that many MMPT groups.
comparison: Current owners name it material/group count; it is not the root texture count and may have a different cardinality.

extractor_claim: Of the 296 CMVB payload bytes, the extractor leaves 283 uninterpreted and describes many as pointers/unknown data.
comparison: Current round-trip tooling measures and retains the same 283 uninterpreted bytes, including nonzero guards, rather than calling them pointers.
priority_follow_up: P4: field naming requires exact loader consumers.

extractor_claim: MMPT contains vBSize, iBSize, index count, vertex count, primitive count, and active as six u32 words.
comparison: Current parsers validate active=1, byte/count arithmetic, primitiveCount=indexCount-2, and cross-group VBUF reuse.

extractor_claim: Each group is ordered MMPT, IBUF, VBUF, TEXR.
comparison: All supported populated groups use this exact sequence and lengths.

extractor_claim: IBUF is indexCount little-endian u16 indices; exported indices add the current flattened vertex offset.
comparison: Current parser validates bounds and keeps indices part-local; adding a flattened offset is only an exporter choice.

extractor_claim: Only group zero carries VBUF bytes; later groups declare/reuse the same vertex table and their VBUF payload is skipped by declared length.
comparison: Current parser proves declaration equality and requires secondary VBUF payloads to be empty.

extractor_claim: Rigid stride 36 is float3 position, float3 normal, packed u32 colour, float U, float V.
comparison: Current complete parser decodes, validates, emits, and byte-round-trips this layout.

extractor_claim: Stride 48 inserts three floats at +0x0C, tentatively guessed as bone weighting.
comparison: Current corpus proves three matrix-palette slots equal BONE-index times three; weighting/blending remains open.
priority_follow_up: P1: recover the three-slot combination/weight rule and bind matrices.

extractor_claim: Exported positions and normals are multiplied by base orientation using the extractor's explicit row/axis formula; positions then add base position.
comparison: Current owners distinguish local base, hierarchy pose, reference instance, and parent composition and test transformed instances.
priority_follow_up: P2: retail parent/runtime composition remains open; do not infer it from the extractor.

extractor_claim: Stored current orientation and offset position are read/loggable but ignored for geometry export.
comparison: Current identity tooling reports stored-current separately and explicitly declines runtime-composition claims.

extractor_claim: TEXR payload is exactly six u32 texture IDs.
comparison: Current parser retains all six raw slots for every group.

extractor_claim: The exporter assigns every index in a group only TEXR slot zero and ignores slots one through five.
comparison: Current tooling preserves all slots, distinguishes 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel, and exposes layer groups; slot-zero diffuse binding is bounded, not complete multitexture semantics.
priority_follow_up: P2: recover remaining TEXR positional/blend semantics before claiming material parity.

extractor_claim: vBSize/iBSize/primitiveCount/active, FVF, and primitiveType are read but not used to reject or branch.
comparison: Current parser validates declaration arithmetic and exact rigid/skinned stride-FVF-topology profiles with can-fail tests.

extractor_claim: Every imported index list is treated as a triangle strip.
comparison: All supported populated groups use topology value 4 and primitiveCount=indexCount-2; broader retail topology support remains open.
priority_follow_up: P3: close every remaining topology/FVF combination against loader branches.

extractor_claim: Triangle-strip conversion seeds indices 0/1/2, then alternates prior-index order by odd/even strip position.
comparison: The retained harness reproduces the algorithm for FBX compatibility; it is not retail rasterization proof.

extractor_claim: Degenerate strip triples are omitted.
comparison: Current exporters use the same survival rule; retail malformed/degenerate behavior is not inferred.

extractor_claim: FBX polygon termination encodes the final index as -(index+1).
comparison: This is standard FBX output encoding and carries no AYA format semantics.

extractor_claim: Export negates Z for positions and normals.
comparison: The retained harness reproduces this coordinate conversion; it is not proof that stored AYA is intrinsically left-handed.

extractor_claim: Export negates texture V while preserving U.
comparison: The retained harness reproduces this FBX convention; stored/rendered UV semantics still require the runtime path.

extractor_claim: The exporter flattens every part/reference into one static FBX Geometry rather than separate objects.
comparison: Current tooling preserves part, hierarchy, reference, animation, and bone structure even when emitting a static OBJ/FBX view.

extractor_claim: No explicit scale normalization is applied before FBX output.
comparison: This is observable exporter behavior, not proof of retail world-unit semantics.

extractor_claim: The FBX library edits a binary BoxWithTextures template rather than constructing a document.
comparison: The retained harness still depends on the template but reads it through a checked source-built parser.

extractor_claim: The template supplies exactly 24 material slots, a hard exporter ceiling.
comparison: The cap belongs to the generic template, not CMSH; the template audit finds 24 Material, 24 Texture, and 24 Video objects.

extractor_claim: Texture and video objects are found by fixed Objects-list positions 2+24+n and 2+48+n.
comparison: The retained harness repeats this brittle template contract but validates object-list bounds.
priority_follow_up: P4: no format work; replace only if the export harness is productized.

extractor_claim: Template metadata is Blender 3.5 generic Cube geometry with Material1..24 and default1.png..default24.png placeholders.
comparison: Deterministic source-built parsing finds one eight-vertex cube, six quads, 24 generic material/texture/video slots, and no game identifier or payload.

extractor_claim: A mesh texture name is reduced to text after the first backslash, then looked up in resources/dxtntextures.
comparison: The retained harness reproduces the lookup exactly; it is a tool convention and loses deeper path components.
priority_follow_up: P4: harden only if continuing to use the legacy exporter.

extractor_claim: Lookup tries meshtex%{name}(0)A1R5G5B5.aya first, then A8R8G8B8 only.
comparison: The measured shelf has five source-format suffixes and current resolution indexes actual files; two-suffix search is incomplete legacy behavior.
priority_follow_up: P3: retire two-suffix-only lookup if the harness becomes user-facing.

extractor_claim: FBX texture output changes .tga to .png, removes meshtex\\, strips spaces, and writes under MeshTextures.
comparison: The retained harness reproduces this lossy naming convention for compatibility; it is not serialized-name semantics.

extractor_claim: After AYA inflation, the payload is treated as DDS and decoded to BGRA bytes for a 32-bpp ARGB PNG.
comparison: Current owners distinguish source-format suffix from stored DDS FourCC and handle uncompressed/DXT paths with explicit dimensions and result checks.

extractor_claim: The texture extractor allocates a fixed 4 MiB pixel buffer and ignores the native decoder return code.
comparison: The current harness allocates width*height*4 with checked arithmetic and requires success plus positive dimensions.

extractor_claim: Upstream DDSTextureUncompress copied height*height*4 bytes; fork pin 53b10b0 changes this to width*height*4 with null/size guards.
comparison: The fork fixes rectangular output but does not make the third-party DDS reader generally safe for hostile data.

extractor_claim: The README says the game's textures were stored as compressed DXT2.
comparison: The complete measured 800-file dxtntextures shelf contains 212 DXT1 and 588 DXT2 DDS files, so DXT2 is common but not universal.

extractor_claim: The extractor does not blend multiple TEXR layers on one primitive.
comparison: Current tooling retains six slots and exposes bounded material groups, but full blend semantics remain open.

extractor_claim: Animations and bones are not exported.
comparison: Current tools decode pose lanes, BONE indices, and palette slots, though blend/interpolation/runtime scheduling remain open.
priority_follow_up: P1: close three-slot skinning and named-clip ownership.

extractor_claim: Some exported primitive normals appear to point in the wrong direction.
comparison: This is an admitted output symptom, not a localized format claim; current tools preserve/round-trip normals but general rendered winding parity is not proved.
priority_follow_up: P3: compare one controlled rendered primitive against stored normals/winding.

extractor_claim: The extractor is not expected to work on every model and catches only the extract-all outer exception.
comparison: Current parser handles all 367 measured streams, emits 366 due one explicit empty placeholder, and round-trips all 367.

extractor_claim: Extract-all enumerates every direct file in data/resources/meshes without an extension filter.
comparison: The retained harness narrows to *.aya and deterministic name order.

extractor_claim: The expected root layout is <game>/data/resources with meshes and dxtntextures children.
comparison: The PC corpus and current tools use this layout; it is not asserted for consoles.

extractor_claim: Both ASCII and binary FBX outputs are enabled by default and independently selectable.
comparison: The retained harness supports both outputs but uses binary-only in corpus export lanes.
